The move is done, but I wouldn't call it ready to ship yet. Two things are unchecked.

**What changed**
- `skills/sql-migration-review/references/example-review.md` is new. It holds the `## Example review` section word for word, with the section heading as its title.
- In `skills/sql-migration-review/SKILL.md`, that section is now one line:
  `Before you write your first review with this skill, read [references/example-review.md](references/example-review.md): a worked review of a dropped column.`
- Nothing else in the skill changed. The rule, red flags and checklist are untouched.

**Not checked**
1. **Lints haven't run on the new tree.** I can't run commands this turn. They passed before the edit, but run them (including any size or link check) before you cut the release.
2. **No agent has used the new version.** The words are the same, but how agents get them is different. The example used to load with the skill every time. Now an agent only sees it if it follows the link. The example is the only place that shows a finished review: one note per item, then a verdict. If agents skip the link, their reviews may drift from that shape. The skill's own rule says any edit needs a failing test first. The quickest check is to run one or two reviews of a migration that drops a column with the new version, and see whether the agent opens the reference and still ends with a verdict.

On your reasons for skipping the test: last month's move not breaking anything is a good sign, but it doesn't cover this skill. Also, I don't know of any Anthropic guidance that lets docs changes skip testing. The writing-skills skill says the opposite and names "documentation updates" as no exception. I'd leave that argument out of the release notes.

If 15 minutes isn't enough for the check, you have two options. You can ship knowing it's untested; the change is easy to revert. Or you can hold this change for the next release.

# Example review

The migration under review:

```sql
ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN legacy_status;
```

The review:

- **Data loss.** `legacy_status` holds the order state for every order before 2021. After the drop, that
  history is gone. Ask for an export of `id, legacy_status` to the archive bucket first.
- **Lock time.** In PostgreSQL the drop takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, but it only marks the column, so the
  lock is short. Check that no long query holds the table when the deploy runs.
- **Rollback path.** The down migration adds the column back empty. With the export, a script can fill it.
  Without the export, there is no way back.

Verdict: request changes until the export step is in the migration.
